UnknownTime-travel significance: 4/10
Research & sources (may contain spoilers)
Catalog assessment
Consulted plot describes recurring patterns and a reenacted historic murder associated with a stellar event, but not a clearly resetting interval or actual time displacement.
Time-travel significance
After a strange freeze at 2:22 lets air traffic controller Dylan avert a mid-air collision, the same sequence of sounds, people and events starts recurring around him at that minute every day, drawing him to Grand Central Station. The pattern links him and Sarah to a 1986 love triangle that ended in murder at Grand Central at 2:22, apparently re-enacting itself through reincarnation, and Dylan races to break it. Recurring time patterns and an echo of the past drive the thriller, but days do not reset, no one travels and the past repeats through fate rather than time travel, so it stays at 4.

In 2044, where an AI-run society treats emotion as a threat, Gabrielle submits to a DNA purification that immerses her in her past lives so their traumas can be erased. The whole film is built from those immersions, intercutting her 1910 Paris life, ending in the Great Flood, and her 2014 Los Angeles life, with Louis returning in every era, the same dread of catastrophe carried across lives, and glitches as the periods bleed into each other. The machine-mediated reliving of other eras shapes the entire narrative, which lifts it well above its provisional 5. It stops short of Mr. Nobody's 8 because these are past incarnations relived from within rather than travel or the same life revisited, and nothing in the past can be changed.
